compound.name: α-thujone
compound.one_liner: Sage's convulsant ketone (10-60 % of the oil); a GABA-A antagonist with an EMA intake limit.

identity.note: PubChem titles this CID 'Thujone', but CAS 546-80-5 and the (1S,4R,5R) stereo are (-)-α-thujone.

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Salvia officinalis L., folium and Salvia officinalis L., aetheroleum, Rev. 1. EMA/HMPC/150801/2015 (20 Sep 2016). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-salvia-officinalis-l-folium-and-salvia-officinalis-l-aetheroleum-revision-1_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: ALPHA-THUJONE Leaf Essent. Oil 200000-363300 ppm; Leaf 200-10172 ppm. | Basis as recorded: % of essential oil

pharmacology.primary_targets: GABA-A receptor chloride channel (non-competitive antagonist, picrotoxinin-like) [39].
pharmacology.mechanism: α-Thujone blocks the GABA-gated chloride channel; toxicity in mice is reversed by benzodiazepines and barbiturates, and it is rapidly detoxified to 7-hydroxy-α-thujone, which is 56-fold less potent [39]. EMA cites clonic seizures in the NTP rat study as the critical endpoint [2].

compound.absorption_bioavailability: Rapid hepatic metabolism to hydroxylated metabolites (in animals) [39]; human PK not researched.

evidence.outcome_summary: Competitive inhibition of channel-blocker binding; receptor suppression in neurons.

evidence.test_article_detail: thujone, NTP 2-year and 14-week rat studies (as summarised by EMA); mouse toxicity
evidence.outcome_summary: Clonic seizures are the critical endpoint for EMA limits.

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

safety_flags.detail: Main toxic constituent of sage oil; epileptiform convulsions reported after prolonged use of alcoholic extracts or pure oil [1].
safety_flags.threshold_or_limit: 3.5 mg/day (rat 14-week NOEL, UF 100) or 6.6 mg/day (NTP benchmark dose); 3-7 mg/day said to pose no special concern; minimise in pregnancy and children
safety_flags.source_citation: EMA/HMPC public statement on thujone, EMA/HMPC/732886/2010 Rev.1 (2012)

compound.teaching_note: The absinthe molecule. Its mechanism was only pinned down in 2000 [39], and today it is why sage products must declare thujone [2].
gaps: Thujone content of a home sage infusion not sourced; the limit applies to herbal medicinal products.
